Round-8 FAIL re-checked from scratch. The comment now reads "Quotients that terminate within eight digits." over (0.8 -> 1.2500000) and (1.6 -> 0.62500000), and "Exact ties at the ninth digit go to even: 1/4096 = 0.000244140625, 1/0.4096 = 2.44140625." over (4096 -> 0.00024414062) and (0.4096 -> 2.4414062). Re-derived with exact Fractions: 1/4096 = 0.000244140625 and 1/0.4096 = 2.44140625 have nine significant digits 244140625, remainder exactly 1/2 at the eighth digit (24414062|5), so both are true ties; half-even gives ...062 (even), half-up ...063; 0.8 and 1.6 give 1.25 and 0.625 (remainder 0), so they are not ties, and the comment says so. Mutation test (scratch copy /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify10-data-tooling/mutbase, never the repo; harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify10-data-tooling/scripts/mutrun.py; results /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify10-data-tooling/out/mut_fetch2.txt, mut_fetch3.txt): ROUND_HALF_EVEN -> ROUND_HALF_UP in both quantize calls is KILLED by test_inversion_keeps_eight_significant_digits_in_plain_decimal[4096-0.00024414062], and each new tie case kills it alone ([0.4096-2.4414062] and [4096-0.00024414062]); round 8 recorded this mutant as surviving all 43 tests. HALF_UP on the first quantize only: killed. ROUND_HALF_DOWN survives, and that is an equivalent mutant: a tie needs a terminating quotient with nine significant digits ending in 5, i.e. a power of 5 with nine digits, and 5^12 = 244140625 is the only one, whose eighth digit is even, so half-even and half-down agree on every tie. HALF_UP on the carry re-quantize only also survives and is equivalent: a carry needs a quotient within 0.05 of a unit of the coarser quantum of the next power of ten, so the second rounding is never an exact half. Observations, none of which changes a snapshot or a tie result: a float-quotient variant Decimal(1.0/float(value)) survives and differs from _invert only on exact ties such as "40960" (0.000024414062 against 0.000024414063; 0 differences on 200,000 random inputs); str(rounded) instead of f"{rounded:f}" survives because no case has a quotient below 1e-6, although the test name says "plain decimal". Optional pins: ("40960", "0.000024414062") and ("20000000", "0.000000050000000").
